title: How to Tell If a Guy Likes You at Work: 20 Telling Signs
h1: How to Tell If a Guy Likes You at Work: 20 Telling Signs (and What to Do)
description: Learn how to tell if a guy likes you at work with 20 obvious and subtle signs, how to separate friendliness from flirting, and how to handle it wisely.
keyword: how to tell if a guy likes you at work
excerpt: Twenty obvious and subtle signs a coworker is into you, how to tell friendliness from flirting, and how to navigate an office crush professionally.
intro:
Workplaces are tricky places to read romantic interest. You see each other every day, you have to be friendly, and everyone is on their best professional behavior. So when a coworker always seems to appear at the coffee machine when you do, it’s hard to know whether he’s interested or just really likes coffee.

This guide breaks down how to tell if a guy likes you at work, with twenty signs ranging from the obvious to the subtle. You’ll also learn how to separate a friendly colleague from an interested one, what to consider before acting on an office crush, and how to respond if the attention isn’t welcome.
body:
Why reading interest at work is harder

At work, people are expected to be helpful, polite and approachable, so behaviors that would signal interest elsewhere can just be good teamwork. Many men are also cautious about flirting at work because of company policies and the risk of making someone uncomfortable. That means signs are often quieter and more indirect.

The key is to compare: does he treat you differently than he treats other coworkers? Look for patterns over weeks, not one friendly afternoon.

Obvious signs he likes you at work

1. He finds excuses to cross paths

He stops by your desk, takes the long way to the printer or seems to need the break room whenever you’re in it. Repeated “coincidences” rarely are.

2. He’s always offering to help

He volunteers to fix your laptop issue, cover a task or proofread your presentation, often before you ask. Effort that goes beyond his job description is a strong signal.

3. You catch him looking at you

In meetings or across the office, you notice his gaze landing on you, and he looks away quickly or smiles when caught.

4. He asks about your love life

Questions like “Big plans with anyone this weekend?” or “Are you seeing someone?” are often a way of checking whether you’re available.

5. He seems to show up wherever you are

Team lunch, happy hour, the company softball game. If you’re going, he’s suddenly going too.

6. He takes lunch when you do

His schedule keeps lining up with yours. He may ask to join you or suggest grabbing food together.

7. You end up on the same shifts or projects a lot

If he has any say in scheduling or project assignments, and you keep landing together, he may be nudging that along.

8. He really wants you at after-work events

He doesn’t just mention happy hour; he personally asks whether you’re coming and seems disappointed if you can’t.

9. He tries to find out if you’re single

He might ask indirectly, mention a coworker’s wedding to gauge your reaction, or ask your work friends about you.

10. You share inside jokes

You have running jokes that nobody else gets. Shared humor is a sign of a special connection.

Stronger signs that go beyond friendliness

11. He reacts strongly when you mention leaving

If you talk about a new job or a transfer and he seems genuinely upset or tries to talk you out of it, you may matter to him more than a typical coworker would.

12. He opens up about his personal life

He tells you about his family, his weekend or his worries. Men often share personal details with people they want to be closer to.

13. He compliments you

He notices when you nail a presentation or get a new haircut. Watch whether his compliments are respectful and specific, and whether he compliments others the same way.

14. He messages you outside work hours

A text about something funny, a meme or a “how was your weekend?” that has nothing to do with work suggests he’s thinking about you off the clock.

15. He gives you his full attention

When you talk, his phone goes away and he faces you. He listens like what you say matters.

16. He seems bothered when you have a date

If you mention seeing someone and he gets quiet or changes the subject, he may be disappointed.

17. He remembers everything you tell him

Your dog’s name, your sister’s visit, your favorite snack. Remembering details is a sign of genuine attention.

Subtle signs he’s into you

  1. His body language shifts around you. He leans in, faces you directly, mirrors your posture or adjusts his hair or clothes when you approach. Our guide to the body language of men covers these cues in detail.
  2. He gets a little nervous. A confident guy who stumbles over words or fidgets only around you may be feeling something.
  3. He makes small, thoughtful gestures. Bringing you a coffee the way you like it, saving you a seat or leaving a snack on your desk.
Tip: Ask a trusted work friend whether they’ve noticed anything. An outside view can confirm whether his behavior toward you stands out, but choose someone discreet so it doesn’t become office gossip.

Friendly coworker or interested guy?

Some signs are clearer than others. Here’s a quick comparison:

  • Likely just friendly: He helps everyone, jokes with the whole team, talks about his partner openly, and only connects with you during work hours.
  • Likely interested: He seeks you out specifically, asks about your relationship status, contacts you after hours, remembers personal details and seems nervous or extra attentive around you.

For more ways to tell the difference, read signs he likes you more than a friend.

Things to think about before acting on an office crush

If you like him back, workplace romance can work, and plenty of couples met at work. A little planning helps protect both of you.

  • Check your company’s policy. Some workplaces require disclosure of relationships, especially between people in the same reporting line.
  • Consider the power dynamic. Dating a manager or someone you supervise is far more complicated and often prohibited.
  • Think about the what-ifs. Could you still work together comfortably if it didn’t work out?
  • Keep it professional on the clock. Discretion protects your reputations and your colleagues’ comfort.

How to show interest back without risking your reputation

If you like him too, you can send gentle signals while staying professional:

  • Linger a little in conversations. Ask about his weekend or follow up on something he mentioned.
  • Accept his invitations to group events. Team lunches and after-work outings are low-pressure ways to spend time together.
  • Smile and hold eye contact. Warm, open body language lets him know his attention is welcome.
  • Keep personal chats off work channels. If you start texting, use personal numbers rather than company messaging tools.
  • Stay focused during work hours. Being great at your job keeps the spotlight on your professionalism, not your love life.

These small signals give him the confidence to make a move without either of you crossing professional lines.

How to find out if he likes you

If the signs are adding up and you’re interested, you can create a low-stakes opening outside of work. Suggest coffee on the weekend or a lunch away from the office. If he jumps at the chance and it feels like a date, you have your answer. Our guide on how to ask someone out can help with wording.

What if the attention isn’t welcome?

Not every bit of interest is wanted, and you never owe anyone a response. If his attention makes you uncomfortable, a clear, polite boundary usually works: “I like working with you, but I’d prefer to keep things professional.”

Tip: If someone keeps pushing after you’ve said no, comments on your body, or uses his position to pressure you, that may be harassment. Document what happens and speak with HR or a manager you trust.

The bottom line

Knowing how to tell if a guy likes you at work comes down to noticing patterns: he seeks you out, helps without being asked, remembers details, asks about your love life and treats you differently than the rest of the team. If you feel the same, move thoughtfully and keep things professional at the office. If you don’t, a kind, clear boundary is always okay. For more signs in non-work settings, see does he like me.
takeaways: Look for patterns of special treatment, not one-off friendliness.
Seeking you out, asking about your love life and after-hours messages are strong signs.
Body language like leaning in, mirroring and nervousness offers subtle clues.
Check company policies and power dynamics before acting on an office crush.
Unwanted attention deserves a clear boundary, and persistent pressure belongs with HR.

faq.q: How do you know if a coworker is flirting with you?
faq.a: Flirting usually shows up as extra attention aimed specifically at you: lingering eye contact, playful teasing, compliments, finding reasons to talk, asking about your relationship status and contacting you outside work. If he behaves this way with you but not with other colleagues, it is likely flirting.

faq.q: Do guys hide their feelings at work?
faq.a: Often, yes. Many men are cautious about romantic interest at work because of company policies, fear of making someone uncomfortable and the risk to their reputation. Their signs may be quieter, such as helping you often, remembering details and seeking out your company in group settings.

faq.q: Is it a good idea to date a coworker?
faq.a: It can work well, especially between peers, but think it through. Review your company policy, avoid relationships with someone in your reporting line, keep things professional at work and consider whether you could still work together comfortably if it ended.

faq.q: What if a coworker likes me but I don’t like him back?
faq.a: Be kind and clear. Something like “I enjoy working with you, but I want to keep things professional” sets a boundary without drama. Avoid mixed signals afterward. If he keeps pushing or makes you uncomfortable, document it and talk to HR.
